skill_traces.query:
Jolene: Hey Deborah, how's it going? Guess what? Yesterday my partner and I got back from an awesome trip to Rio de Janeiro- we checked out some cool yoga classes.
Deborah: That yoga pose looks great. Must've been a cool experience for the two of you. What did the trip teach you?
Jolene: This country was awesome! It showed me different kinds of yoga and their backgrounds, which made me appreciate it even more. We visited a lot of delicious cafes! Have you ever been somewhere that was important to you?
Deborah: Yep, last month I visited my mom`s house which holds a special place in my heart. My mom had good and bad times there, but it's still a symbol of her strength and the love she shared with me. This is my husband in front of this house.
Jolene: What was it like?
Deborah: It brought back fond memories as I relaxed outside.
Jolene: Sounds great! So glad you have a place to relax and find peace.
Deborah: Thanks, Jolene. It's special for me. How about you? Is there a place that helps you relax?
Jolene: I go to this nearby place to meditate by a tranquil spot.
Deborah: Looks chill. What's been the effect of that?
Jolene: It helps me make sense of everything and relieves stress. It's like a restart.
Deborah: Cool, glad you found a place to chill. We all need that occasionally. This is one of my favorite spots to ponder and let things go.

Jolene: Looks great! What made you pick that spot?
Deborah: The soothing vibes and nice views made it ideal for reflecting and letting go.
Jolene: Here is one more photo from Rio de Janeiro. We went on many excursions there.
Deborah: Wow, those stairs look cool! Where were they taken?
Jolene: We had a great time visiting an old temple. The stairs were amazing!
Deborah: Wow, exploring those temples must have been incredible! Three years ago I was also in Rio de Janeiro, I took a beautiful photo on one of the excursions.
Jolene: The architecture and history of it all were really interesting. I'm sure you also liked the places you visited there!
Deborah: Exploring historical places and learning their stories is so fun. It was a great experience. I want to share this photo with you.
Jolene:  By the way, what did that paper have written on it in the photo?
Deborah: This was written to me by a friend who, unfortunately, will never be able to support me. I miss him here. This quote says"Let go of what no longer serves you."
Jolene: I'm sorry! That's a good reminder to stay focused and let go of what no longer serves us. Remember the quote in my notebook? It also inspires me!
Deborah: What other quotes give you strength?
Jolene: I came across this one while browsing and it really hit home with me. It's a great reminder to ditch the negative stuff and focus on growing and being positive.
Deborah: Surrounding ourselves with good stuff and striving to improve is key.
Jolene: Yep, Deborah! It's about creating a good atmosphere to help us grow and improve. By the way, I have a new plant.
Deborah: What made you pick it?
Jolene: I got this as a reminder to nurture myself and embrace fresh starts.
Deborah: Nice job, Jolene! Take care of yourself and embrace new beginnings.
Jolene: Thanks Deb! Will do. Good talking to you. Take care!
Deborah: Have a great day!

nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: AggregateRepeatedVisitCounts
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message shows a person visiting a place and existing memories record an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, create or update a memory stating the total number of visits.
content: During extraction, when a message states that a person visited a place and another message in the session already establishes an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, generate a candidate memory containing the cumulative number of visits; do not expand this to other places or trips.

During CRUD, when adding or updating a visit event, search the retrieved memory pool for prior visits by the same person to the same place; if found, add a compact visit-count memory or update the existing one so the total count is explicit.
Only aggregate same-person, same-place visits; do not count different locations, do not add a count memory when no prior visit exists, and stop once the count is recorded.

content: If the speaker reports attending, visiting, or participating in an event and provides a time reference, create an event candidate memory.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
Store only the explicit details; do not infer a specific event type.
Stop after capturing the known event facts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Past Completed Activities as Events
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message includes a relative past-time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month') describing an activity like reading, watching, or visiting.
content: When a user states they did something in the past with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'two weeks ago', 'last month', 'in January'), resolve the time from the message/session timestamp and record it as a completed event memory (e.g., 'read X in January 2023'), never as a current state, preference, or 'currently reading/watching/using' memory.
Do not merge a past completed activity with an ongoing current activity into a single memory; keep separate memories with distinct time spans and completion status.
Stop after creating the past event memory; do not expand to other activities unless explicitly mentioned.
